challenges.title: Ride the Bull
challenges.intro: Economists are cheerful and companies are hiring. Make the most of a rising market.
challenges.lesson: In a bull market the biggest risk is sitting in cash: missing the climb costs more than any dip.

challenges.title: Survive the Crash
challenges.intro: You start fully invested in the whole market (MKT100). Rumour says stocks are overheated… keep an eye on the fear gauge.
challenges.lesson: A crash hits almost everything at once. Diversification can't remove market-wide risk; only cash or calmer assets soften it.

challenges.title: Bear Market Blues
challenges.intro: The economy is wobbling. Stay invested, but don't let a long slide wreck you.
challenges.lesson: Defensive companies (drinks, groceries, medicine) usually fall less in a bear market because people still buy them.

challenges.title: Tech Wreck
challenges.intro: You start with everything in TECH3, a fund of three tech giants. A fund is diversified… right?
challenges.lesson: A sector fund holds many companies but only one kind of risk. Real diversification means different sectors.

challenges.title: Sideways Shuffle
challenges.intro: The market can't make up its mind. Finish in profit without feeding the broker.
challenges.lesson: In a choppy market, frequent trading mostly pays fees. Patience is a strategy.

challenges.title: Beat the Market
challenges.intro: Professional fund managers try to beat the index every year. Can you?
challenges.lesson: Most professional funds fail to beat a simple index fund over time, mainly because of fees and bad timing.

challenges.title: The Rollercoaster
challenges.intro: A crash in the first week, then a long, slow recovery. Keep your drawdown small and still finish ahead.
challenges.lesson: Big early losses need even bigger gains to recover: −20% needs +25% to get back to even.

challenges.title: Margin Madness
challenges.intro: You've gone all in on the whole market (MKT100) with 3× leverage: two thirds of it is borrowed. The economy looks shaky…
challenges.lesson: Leverage multiplies a fall too. Cutting the loan early (sell some, then leverage 1) is the only reliable way to dodge a margin call.

challenges.title: Borrowed Bull
challenges.intro: Jobs are up and loans are cheap. Can borrowed money (try leverage 2) turn a good market into a great result without a margin call?
challenges.lesson: In a steady rise, modest leverage really does multiply gains, minus the interest. The same bet in a falling market would have doubled the losses.
